item.title: Chinese defense minister calls for deeper cooperation on global security
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-16
BEIJING, Sept. 15 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese military is willing to work with all parties to deepen practical cooperation, jointly address global security challenges, and resolutely safeguard world and regional peace and stability, Minister of National Defense Dong Jun said on Tuesday. Dong made the remarks during separate meetings in Beijing with defense officials from Myanmar, Brunei, Belarus, Azerbaijan, Kyrgyzstan and Armenia, as well as ASEAN Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn, who are in Beijing to attend the 13th Beijing Xiangshan Forum, which is scheduled to run from Tuesday to Thursday. Dong welcomed the guests to the Beijing Xiangshan Forum, saying that over the past 20 years, the forum has upheld the principles of equality, openness, inclusiveness and mutual learning, contributing wisdom to promoting peace and cooperation and advancing common security. He said that amid growing instability and uncertainty in the international landscape, the Chinese military is ready to work with all parties to implement the vision of a community with a shared future for humanity and the four major global initiatives. Themed "Build Consensus on Stability, Advance Security Governance Together," this year's forum has drawn attendees from almost 100 countries, regions and international organizations. Over the past two decades, the forum has evolved into a vital international public good, offering a space for equal dialogue and joint efforts toward global peace.

item.title: China ready to share military building experience as PLA approaches centenary, says defense minister
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-16
BEIJING, Sept. 16 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Defense Minister Dong Jun said on Wednesday that the Chinese military stands ready to share its experience in building the armed forces as the People's Liberation Army (PLA) approaches its 100th anniversary. "As the Chinese military is about to mark its centenary, we are accelerating our modernization drive. We stand ready to share our experience and philosophy in building and governing the armed forces with all parties," Dong said at the opening ceremony of the 13th Beijing Xiangshan Forum. Dong added that the Chinese military is also willing to provide assistance to countries in need to the best of its ability. The PLA was founded in the Nanchang Uprising on Aug. 1, 1927, which marked the beginning of the Communist Party of China's independent leadership of the revolutionary war. Dong said that the Chinese military is also willing to work with all parties to deliver more tangible outcomes, and achieve mutual success and secure a win-win future through practical cooperation. In the face of sudden and frequent natural disasters, the Chinese military is willing to do its utmost and extend a helping hand where needed, Dong said. "We will actively carry out joint disaster relief early warning, emergency response, humanitarian assistance, and public security cooperation, and support the development and security of all countries through concrete actions," said Dong.

item.title: Xi congratulates Jilin University on 80th founding anniversary
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-16
BEIJING, Sept. 16 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday sent a congratulatory letter to Jilin University, celebrating its 80th founding anniversary. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, extended congratulations to the faculty, students and alumni of the university. He urged the university to carry forward the revolutionary traditions, leverage its comprehensive strengths, focus on the country's strategic needs, cultivate more high-caliber talent, and make greater contributions to the full revitalization of the Northeast in the new era and to advancing Chinese modernization.

item.title: Philippines' claim of so-called maritime jurisdiction over China's territory is illegal: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-15
BEIJING, Sept. 15 (Xinhua) -- Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Tuesday that the Philippines' claim of so-called maritime jurisdiction over China's territory is illegal. Guo made the remarks at a regular press briefing, adding that China will continue to take resolute measures to safeguard its territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests, and firmly oppose any infringement. It is reported that in a statement issued on Sept. 11, the Philippines' Department of Foreign Affairs reaffirmed the Philippines' sovereign rights and jurisdiction over Meiji Jiao and Zhubi Jiao as low-tide elevations (LTE) within the Philippines' exclusive economic zone and continental shelf. Later, it changed the narrative, reaffirming its sovereignty over Zhubi Jiao as an LTE within the territorial sea of Zhongye Dao. "Nansha Qundao, including Meiji Jiao, Zhubi Jiao and Zhongye Dao, are China's inherent territory. It is totally legitimate and lawful for China to conduct construction and other activities on its own territory, a matter within China's sovereignty," Guo said. He said the territorial scope of the Philippines has already been defined by a series of international treaties. Nansha Qundao has never been part of the Philippine territory, Guo stressed. "According to the 'land dominates the sea' principle in international law, the Philippines' claim of so-called maritime jurisdiction over China's territory is illegal," said Guo, adding the Philippine side at one point claimed that Zhubi Jiao is within its exclusive economic zone (EEZ) and continental shelf, but later claimed that it lies within the territorial sea of the island it illegally occupies. "This only exposes how absurd and random its claim is, making it totally untenable," the spokesperson noted. He said the "South China Sea arbitration" is completely a political manipulation by the Philippines to grab unlawful gains. The so-called "award" is illegal, null and void, and has no binding force, Guo added. Noting the Philippines' so-called "Maritime Zones Act" illegally includes China's Huangyan Dao and most of the islands and reefs in Nansha Qundao and relevant waters into the Philippines' maritime zone, Guo said this is a grave violation of China's territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests in the South China Sea, and is illegal and null and void. "China firmly opposes it and will never accept it," said Guo, adding the Philippines should immediately stop infringing upon China's rights, and stop the provocations and publicity stunts.

item.title: China urges U.S. to stop expanding military build-up in outer space: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-15
BEIJING, Sept. 15 (Xinhua) -- China urges the United States to stop expanding military build-up in outer space, and uphold global strategic stability with concrete actions, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Tuesday. Guo made the remarks at a regular press briefing in response to the U.S. confirmation that it has weapons deployed in space. Guo added that China stands for peaceful use of outer space and keeping it safe, and opposes any arms race in outer space or any attempt to weaponize it and turn it into a war zone.
